requirement:
For a response with exactly one `submit_result` call, arguments other than an
object containing only the `result` field receive a tool error describing that
expected structure. The model can resubmit in the same conversation. Decoding
the field's value into `R` follows
{cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.agent-calls.judge.submission.decoding`.
rationale:
structural: `requirements.sdk.graph.agent-harness.submission.invalid` states only observable behavior. For a response with exactly one `submit_result` call, any arguments other than an object containing only the `result` field get a tool error that describes the expected structure. The model can then resubmit in the same conversation. A different implementation could validate the arguments with a hand-written check, a schema validator, or a serde struct with `deny_unknown_fields`. It could build the error text in any way. All of these give the same behavior, so none of them violates a clause. The text names no required library, algorithm, signature, type, field or delegation interface. The sentence about decoding the field's value into `R` only cites `requirements.sdk.graph.agent-calls.judge.submission.decoding`. That requirement supplies context, and its obligations are judged on their own. The requirement has no implementation edges, and no review roots were supplied. Since no structural obligation needs implementation evidence, nothing is missing.

behavioral: Obligations for `requirements.sdk.graph.agent-harness.submission.invalid`: (1) With exactly one `submit_result` call, any arguments other than an object containing only `result` produce a tool error describing the expected structure. (2) The model can resubmit in the same conversation. (3) Decoding the field's value into `R` follows the cited `requirements.sdk.graph.agent-calls.judge.submission.decoding`.

Coverage:
- Envelope validation: `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/tools.rs#mod[submission_tests]/fn[submission_envelopes_require_one_result_field]` checks the error message for non-object arguments (null, array, string, bool), `{}`, a wrong field name, and `result` plus an extra field. It also checks that a valid envelope returns the inner value unchanged, including null and other odd values.
- Tool-error delivery and resubmission: `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/tests.rs#fn[malformed_submissions_receive_feedback_and_can_be_corrected]` runs a scripted agent through `{}`, `{"other":true}` and `{"result":{},"extra":true}`. Each is followed by a valid second submission. The test asserts the following:
  - The next request's last message is a ToolResult with `is_error` set.
  - The feedback contains the envelope-structure guidance.
  - The second submission succeeds in the same conversation, with the vetting callback called once.
- Decoding failures (the cited requirement): the same test covers missing field, string-encoded JSON, an unknown variant and a wrong type. It asserts the decoding diagnostic and the schema guidance appear as a tool error, and that vetting is invoked only for the decoded answer. The cited decoding requirement's own obligations are not reassessed here.

The non-object argument shapes are tested at the `submitted_value` unit level. The scripted agent test exercises only object-shaped invalid arguments through the full flow. `submitted_value` is the one envelope check, so the unit test plus the end-to-end error and resubmission test cover the obligations. I found no unmarked relevant tests and no gaps.

text: For a response with exactly one `submit_result` call, arguments other than an
object containing only the `result` field receive a tool error describing that
expected structure. The model can resubmit in the same conversation. Decoding
Decode the submitted `result` directly as `R` and invoke vetting callbacks only
for successfully decoded answers. If decoding fails, return the decoding error
and guidance on the expected `result` to the model as a tool error. Keep the
conversation open for a corrected submission.
